## Setting up API key
The [Google Distance Matrix API](https://mapsplatform.google.com/) requires registration, and an API key is required in each function call. It is possible to store the key for duration of a R session by using `gmapsdistance::set.api.key()` call.

Note that in order to keep the maintainers API key private it has been stored locally in an environment variable; in the most frequent use cases it can be used in plain text.


``` r
library(gmapsdistance)
set.api.key(Sys.getenv("GOOGLE_API_KEY"))
```

## Distance between cities
In this example we will compute the driving distance between Washington DC, and New York City. The code returns the `Time`, the `Distance` and the `Status` of the query (`OK` if it was successful). The calculation will be made using the "driving" method, which is the default.


``` r
results = gmapsdistance(origin = "Washington DC",
                        destination = "New York City NY")
results
## $Distance
## [1] 361969
## 
## $Time
## [1] 14096
## 
## $Status
## [1] "OK"
```

## Walking distance between GPS coordinates
In this example we will compute the walking distance between the Greek cities of
Marathon and Athens. We show that the function is able to handle LAT-LONG coordinates.


``` r
results = gmapsdistance(origin = "38.1621328 24.0029257",
                        destination = "37.9908372 23.7383394",
                        mode = "walking")
results
## $Distance
## [1] 39459
## 
## $Time
## [1] 33278
## 
## $Status
## [1] "OK"
```

## Distance matrix at a specific departure time
This example computes the travel distance and time matrices between two vectors of cities at a specific departure time

``` r
results = gmapsdistance(origin = c("Washington DC", "New York NY",
                                   "Seattle WA", "Miami FL"),
                        destination = c("Los Angeles CA", "Austin TX",
                                        "Chicago IL", "Philadelphia PA"),
                        mode = "bicycling",
                        # departure time as seconds from Unix Epoch (1970-01-01)
                        departure = 1795040400)
results
## $Distance
##               Los Angeles CA Austin TX Chicago IL Philadelphia PA
## Washington DC        4988399   3103873    1284099          338482
## New York NY          5238350   3353824    1534050          162117
## Seattle WA           2123997   3841398    3654494         5089729
## Miami FL             4910272   2517696    2476761         2341252
## 
## $Time
##               Los Angeles CA Austin TX Chicago IL Philadelphia PA
## Washington DC         923026    583510     247214           67429
## New York NY           971965    632448     296152           32252
## Seattle WA            413012    720116     687405          965463
## Miami FL              900337    459925     475143          439673
## 
## $Status
##               Los Angeles CA Austin TX Chicago IL Philadelphia PA
## Washington DC "OK"           "OK"      "OK"       "OK"           
## New York NY   "OK"           "OK"      "OK"       "OK"           
## Seattle WA    "OK"           "OK"      "OK"       "OK"           
## Miami FL      "OK"           "OK"      "OK"       "OK"
# Equivalently
results = gmapsdistance(origin = c("Washington DC", "New York NY",
                                   "Seattle WA", "Miami FL"),
                        destination = c("Los Angeles CA", "Austin TX",
                                        "Chicago IL", "Philadelphia PA"),
                        mode = "bicycling",
                        dep_date = "2026-11-18",
                        dep_time = "22:20:00")
results
```

## Long format of distance matrix
This example computes the travel distance and time matrices between two vectors of cities and return the results in long format

``` r

destination = c("Los Angeles CA", "Austin TX", "Chicago IL")

results = gmapsdistance(origin,

                        shape = "long")
```

## Distance matrix between GPS coordinates
This example computes the travel distance and time between two vectors of cities defined as LAT-LONG coordinates.


``` r
origin = c("40.431478 -80.0505401", "33.7678359 -84.4906438")
destination = c("43.0995629 -79.0437609", "41.7096483 -86.9093986")

results = gmapsdistance(origin,
                        destination,
                        mode="bicycling",
                        shape="long")

results
## $Distance
##                       or                     de Distance
## 1  40.431478 -80.0505401 43.0995629 -79.0437609   439271
## 2 33.7678359 -84.4906438 43.0995629 -79.0437609  1634122
## 3  40.431478 -80.0505401 41.7096483 -86.9093986   723665
## 4 33.7678359 -84.4906438 41.7096483 -86.9093986  1207443
## 
## $Time

## 2 33.7678359 -84.4906438 43.0995629 -79.0437609 321476
## 3  40.431478 -80.0505401 41.7096483 -86.9093986 137806
## 4 33.7678359 -84.4906438 41.7096483 -86.9093986 238316
## 
## $Status
##                       or                     de status
## 1  40.431478 -80.0505401 43.0995629 -79.0437609     OK
```

## Combination of distances
This example computes the travel distance and time between two vectors of cities using the 'combinations' option.


``` r
# 1. Pairwise

or = c("Washington DC", "New York NY", "Seattle WA", "Miami FL")
des = c("Los Angeles CA", "Austin TX", "Chicago IL", "Philadelphia PA")

results = gmapsdistance(origin = or,
                        destination = des,
                        mode = "bicycling",
                        combinations = "pairwise")
results
## $Distance
##              or              de Distance
## 1 Washington DC  Los Angeles CA  4988399
## 2   New York NY       Austin TX  3353824
## 3    Seattle WA      Chicago IL  3654494
## 4      Miami FL Philadelphia PA  2341252
## 
## $Time
##              or              de   Time
## 1 Washington DC  Los Angeles CA 923026
## 2   New York NY       Austin TX 632448
## 3    Seattle WA      Chicago IL 687405
## 4      Miami FL Philadelphia PA 439673
## 
## $Status
##              or              de status
## 1 Washington DC  Los Angeles CA     OK
## 2   New York NY       Austin TX     OK
## 3    Seattle WA      Chicago IL     OK
## 4      Miami FL Philadelphia PA     OK

# 2. All combinations of origins and destinations in wide format
results = gmapsdistance(origin = or,
                        destination = des,
                        mode = "bicycling",
                        combinations = "all",
                        shape = "wide")
results
```

## Using optional parameters - traffic model and avoidance
This example show the use of traffic model and avoidance parameters, while setting the API key directly in function call.
Note that in order to keep the maintainers API key private it has been stored locally in an environment variable; in the most frequent use cases it can be used in plain text.


``` r
APIkey <- Sys.getenv("GOOGLE_API_KEY") # your actual API key would go here...

# Time and distance using a 'pessimistic' traffic model.
results = gmapsdistance(origin = c("Washington DC", "New York NY"),
                        destination = c("Los Angeles CA", "Austin TX"),
                        mode = "driving",
                        dep_date = "2026-11-14",
                        dep_time = "23:13:20",
                        traffic_model = "pessimistic",
                        shape = "long",
                        key=APIkey)
results
## $Distance
##              or             de Distance
## 1 Washington DC Los Angeles CA  4295052
## 2   New York NY Los Angeles CA  4489237
## 3 Washington DC      Austin TX  2452122
## 4   New York NY      Austin TX  2803898
## 
## $Time
##              or             de   Time
## 1 Washington DC Los Angeles CA 140529
## 2   New York NY Los Angeles CA 148031
## 3 Washington DC      Austin TX  91907
## 4   New York NY      Austin TX 104053
## 
## $Status
##              or             de status
## 1 Washington DC Los Angeles CA     OK
## 2   New York NY Los Angeles CA     OK
## 3 Washington DC      Austin TX     OK
## 4   New York NY      Austin TX     OK

# Time and distance avoiding 'tolls'.
results = gmapsdistance(origin = c("Washington DC", "New York NY"),
                        destination = c("Los Angeles CA", "Austin TX"),
                        mode = "driving",
                        avoid = "tolls",
                        key=APIkey)

results
## $Distance
##               Los Angeles CA Austin TX
## Washington DC        4302046   2459394
## New York NY          4615847   2838349
## 
## $Time
##               Los Angeles CA Austin TX
## Washington DC         140964     81332
## New York NY           154670     95590
## 
## $Status
##               Los Angeles CA Austin TX
## Washington DC "OK"           "OK"     
## New York NY   "OK"           "OK"
```

## Using "foreign" place names
It is perfectly possible to use names in non-ASCII characters; care must be however made that all characters are encoded in UTF-8 though. This may not be the obvious first choice of encoding, especially in Windows environments.


``` r
results = gmapsdistance(origin = "вулиця Хрещатик, Київ",
                        destination = "Майдан Незалежності, Київ",
                        mode = "walking")
results
## $Distance
## [1] 445
## 
## $Time
## [1] 376
## 
## $Status
## [1] "OK"
```

## Using Routes API

The original `gmapsdistance()` function uses [Distance Matrix API](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/distance-matrix/overview), which has transitioned to Legacy status and since October 2026 can no longer be used for new projects.

As a consequence a new implementation was introduced that maps to the new [Routes API](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/routes) platform, which is the new best practice. It is done in a separate function `distance_routes()`, so that the existing `gmapsdistance()` implementation can be kept in place for backward compatibility. `gmapsdistance()` may be deprecated in a future version of the package.

The new implementation follows existing conventions as closely as practical, with some differences - namely the travel modes follow new naming conventions (all UPPERCASE) and the output is now a data frame with one row per origin-destination pair.


``` r
results <- distance_routes(origin = "Washington DC",
                           destination = "New York City NY")
results
##          origin      destination  mode status distance_text distance_value duration_base
## 1 Washington DC New York City NY DRIVE     OK        362 km         361969         14096
##   duration_traffic
## 1            14096
```
The new function supports only pairwise combinations of origins and destinations, and unlike the original one does not provide option of a matrix output or all combinations.


``` r
or <- c("Washington DC", "New York NY", "Seattle WA", "Miami FL")
des <- c("Los Angeles CA", "Austin TX", "Chicago IL", "Philadelphia PA")

results <- distance_routes(origin = or,
                           destination = des,
                           mode = "BICYCLE")
results
##          origin     destination    mode status distance_text distance_value duration_base
## 1 Washington DC  Los Angeles CA BICYCLE     OK      4,988 km        4988399        923026
## 2   New York NY       Austin TX BICYCLE     OK      3,354 km        3353823        632448
## 3    Seattle WA      Chicago IL BICYCLE     OK      3,654 km        3654493        687405
## 4      Miami FL Philadelphia PA BICYCLE     OK      2,341 km        2341252        439673
##   duration_traffic
## 1           923026
## 2           632448
## 3           687405
## 4           439673
```
Most of the arguments have stayed the same, with some differences. Notably the departure (and arrival) date and time has been changed to a single `POSIXct` argument (defaulting to current computer's timezone, possibly giving unintended results).

The output reports two travel times: `duration_base` is the time without considering traffic, and `duration_traffic` the time in traffic. The two are the same unless traffic is considered - that is when a `traffic_model` is given, or a departure time for a trip by road (modes `DRIVE`, `TWO_WHEELER` and `TRUCK`).


``` r
APIkey <- Sys.getenv("GOOGLE_API_KEY") # your actual API key would go here...

# pairwise: Washington DC -> Los Angeles CA, New York NY -> Austin TX
# Time and distance using a 'pessimistic' traffic model.
results <- distance_routes(origin = c("Washington DC", "New York NY"),
                           destination = c("Los Angeles CA", "Austin TX"),
                           mode = "DRIVE",
                           departure = as.POSIXct("2026-11-14 23:13:20", tz = "America/New_York"),
                           traffic_model = "PESSIMISTIC",
                           key=APIkey)
results
##          origin    destination  mode status distance_text distance_value duration_base
## 1 Washington DC Los Angeles CA DRIVE     OK      4,295 km        4295051        140529
## 2   New York NY      Austin TX DRIVE     OK      2,804 km        2803890         93207
##   duration_traffic
## 1           158915
## 2           103660

# Time and distance avoiding 'tolls'.
results <- distance_routes(origin = c("Washington DC", "New York NY"),
                           destination = c("Los Angeles CA", "Austin TX"),
                           mode = "DRIVE",
                           avoid = "tolls",
                           key=APIkey)
results
##          origin    destination  mode status distance_text distance_value duration_base
## 1 Washington DC Los Angeles CA DRIVE     OK      4,302 km        4302046        140964
## 2   New York NY      Austin TX DRIVE     OK      2,838 km        2838349         95590
##   duration_traffic
## 1           140964
## 2            95590
```

Additionally the origin and destination specifications using coordinates require a comma between latitude and longitude, unlike the space accepted by `gmapsdistance()`.


``` r
results <- distance_routes(origin = "38.1621328,24.0029257",
                           destination = "37.9908372,23.7383394",
                           mode = "WALK")
results
##                  origin           destination mode status distance_text distance_value duration_base
## 1 38.1621328,24.0029257 37.9908372,23.7383394 WALK     OK       39.5 km          39459         33278
##   duration_traffic
## 1            33278
```
